terms.gloss: cheap lodging, tavern, a hole in the wall
terms.comment: A humble dwelling, and a low inn or tavern (Petronius, the Digest; Lewis & Short); also a stable.

phrases.latin: Ecquid locī est duōbus? — Est cubiculum duōrum lectōrum.
phrases.english: Is there any room for two? — There’s a double room.
I’ve booked us a room at the hotel.

phrases.latin: quia nōn erat eīs locus in dīversōriō
phrases.english: because there was no room for them in the inn

phrases.latin: Cubiculum nostrum in tertiō tabulātō est.
phrases.english: Our room is on the third floor.

phrases.latin: Ecce cubiculum nostrum! Uter lectus tuus erit?
phrases.english: Here’s our room! Which bed will be yours?

sources: Lewis & Short: deversorium · Lewis & Short: hospitium
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 174, 306, 328, 329.

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
